summary: Built by the Big Ivy CCC camp in 1934 on Little Snowball Mountain, retired in 1980, taken apart by Lloyd Allen, and re-erected at Big Ivy Historical Park in Barnardsville, NC.

facts.design: 21-foot steel-frame tower with a 14x14-foot live-in cab
facts.status_note: The tower standing today is a reconstruction at Big Ivy Historical Park; the original mountain-top tower was taken down

access.note: Reconstructed tower is in Big Ivy Historical Park, Barnardsville; hours not reliably published, so call ahead. The original site is reached only on foot

visit.trail_note: Original mountain site: 7+ mile round-trip hike from Beetree Gap along the Snowball Trail; four concrete blocks remain

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Pisgah National Forest) originally; Big Ivy Historical Society now runs the park where the tower stands

events.note: Built by the Big Ivy CCC camp; the Forest Service decided on the lookout in 1934
Cling Fabe Webb took over the tower (Big Ivy blog); Mote Allen was the first lookout, with no start year given
Forest Service decommissioned the tower after aircraft took over fire detection
Lloyd Allen bought it for $300 and dismantled it by hand; Big Ivy says he removed it around 1985
Reassembled at Big Ivy Historical Park and dedicated in 2007 after a year of volunteer labor; Get Up and Go Camping says re-erected in 2006

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Get Up and Go Camping and dwhike put the Forest Service decommissioning and the $300 sale in 1980; Big Ivy says Lloyd Allen removed the tower around 1985; the registry says volunteers dismantled it in the 1980s. We give 1980 as the decommission year and leave the removal as 1980 to about 1985.
Get Up and Go Camping gives 2006 for re-erection; Big Ivy gives a 2007 dedication after a year of volunteer labor. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Core facts (1934 build, CCC, two staff members, 1980 retirement, $300 sale, reconstruction at Big Ivy) agree across sources. Removal and re-erection years conflict and are reported as ranges. The record's coordinates (35.76112, -82.43127) and elevation (701 m) may describe the reconstructed tower at Big Ivy rather than the original mountain site, so check which place the record means before publishing. Park hours and whether the tower can be climbed are not stated in any source read. The registry's 'standing' is true only of the reconstruction; the original tower is gone.
